text:
lina.design: Quick design review for the Usage & Billing page. Two new alternatives in figma: Timeline view (left) vs Project heatmap grid (right). TL;DR: timeline = better for trend analysis, heatmap = denser at-a-glance for many projects. Which should be primary for orgs that care about monthly billing? :thinking:

lina.design: Key differences I'm trying to resolve: 1) granularity control (Daily / Weekly / Monthly) placement 2) currency selector and whether cost is shown by default or as toggle 3) CSV & invoice export columns and naming 4) token breakdown microcopy and whether we show token counts or only cost.

zack.finance: For finance users, default to Monthly with currency visible. CSV needs columns: `project_id, project_name, start_date, end_date, billable_tokens, embedding_tokens, cached_tokens, usd_amount`. Also include `cost_per_token` if available. Filename example: `redwood-invoice-2026-03-orgname.csv`.

jon.frontend: heatmap has perf benefits for hundreds of projects (canvas rasterize). Timeline needs streaming updates for near-realtime dashboards which is slightly heavier. Both feasible; heatmap needs virtualization and simpler DOM.

priya.content: microcopy on token breakdown should be plain english. Proposal:

```
Billable token usage: tokens consumed for text generation plus system overhead. Embeddings and cached responses are billed separately and not counted here.
```

Make sure to avoid jargon like "KV cache" in UI copy.

matt.pm: Decision proposal: Default = Timeline for orgs with <15 projects, Heatmap for >=15. Show cost by default when org billing currency is set (otherwise show tokens). Granularity toggle in top-left next to timeframe selector. CSV + invoice export should be available in header as a dropdown (Export → CSV / PDF).

lina.design: Two accessibility nits: 1) color palette for heatmap must be colorblind-safe (avoid red/green) and have a separate texture/stripe pattern option for print/PDF 2) granularity toggle must be reachable via keyboard with clear aria-pressed state.

aria-ux-bot: accessibility check results: recommend ColorBrewer `YlOrBr` palette variant + patterned fills for high-density cells. Also add `aria-live=\"polite\"` region for CPU/spend spikes when timeline updates so screenreaders get notified. Ensure toggle has `role=\"tablist\"` semantics when used with mutually exclusive options.

zack.finance: on invoices: include a short description field in the invoice metadata (free text) because customers often need that for accounting. Also add `currency_code` and `exchange_rate_at_invoice_time` to exports.

jon.frontend: implementation note: CSV header we can emit:

```
Project ID,Project Name,Period Start,Period End,Billable Token Usage,Embedding Token Usage,Cached Token Usage,Currency,Cost,Cost Per Token,Invoice ID
```

I'll add a feature flag for `export_extended_csv` in case we want phased rollout.

priya.content: tone for small helper under granularity toggle: `Choose how granular your usage is displayed. Monthly is recommended for billing reconciliation.` keeps it short.

lina.design: about showing cost vs tokens: show a small toggle on the right of the header `Show costs` (persisted per-user). When costs are hidden show token numbers with a subtle USD icon disabled.

matt.pm: timeline vs heatmap rollout plan: ship timeline default + granularity toggle next sprint. Heatmap + CSV extended exports in following sprint. Need acceptance criteria: export schema matches finance request, color palette meets contrast + colorblind checks, toggle keyboard nav works, aria-live announcements for spikes.

action: lina.design will update figma with heatmap patterns and timeline tooltip copy. jon.frontend will prototype CSV export headers + feature flag. zack.finance will validate export sample. priya.content will finalize helper copy. aria-ux-bot will run a11y checklist pre-ship.

lina.design: small copy suggestion for timeline tooltip hover:

`Project: {{project_name}}\nPeriod: {{start}} - {{end}}\nBillable token usage: {{tokens}}\nCost: {{currency}}{{amount}} (if shown)`

jon.frontend: will use that. I'll also make sure the tooltip is readable on keyboard focus and not only hover.

matt.pm: any objections? If none, I'll mark this approved-for-implementation with timeline-first approach.

priya.content: approve from content. Small ask: in CSV export docs mention that `cost_per_token` is derived and may vary by model mix.

zack.finance: approve from finance pending verification of `exchange_rate_at_invoice_time` presence.

aria-ux-bot: reminder: test with NVDA + VoiceOver + keyboard-only. Also run Color Contrast Analyzer and a colorblind simulation (deuteranopia/protanopia).

lina.design: thanks everyone — I'll push updated assets and the final copy strings by EOD. :sparkles:
